Rashi on Pesachim 16b:10:1.hebrew: בשר קדש - שרץ, לשון ״קדש היה בארץ״ (מלכים א יד) — טומאה. והיה חגי הנביא בודק את הכהנים בשנת שתים לדריוש, שהיה בבנין בית שני, לידע אם בקיאין בהלכות טומאה, לפי שנשתכח מהן בגולה, שלא נתעסקו בה בקדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:10:1.english: Hallowed flesh - [This refers to] a creeping animal — an expression [similar to] "there was also a cult prostitute in the land" (I Kings 14:24), [meaning] impurity. And Haggai the prophet was testing the priests in the second year of Darius, which was during the construction of the Second Temple, to know whether they were proficient in the laws of impurity, because they had been forgotten by them in exile, since they had not dealt with consecrated items there.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:10:2.hebrew: ונגע בכנפו - באותו כנף שהשרץ בו, כלומר: השרץ עצמו. ועל כרחך הכי הוא, דאי משום כנף שהוא ראשון — כוליה בגד נמי ראשון הוי, ומאי איריא דנקיט כנף? אלא משום שרץ, שהשרץ עצמו נגע אל הלחם, והלחם אל הנזיד, והנזיד אל היין, והיין אל השמן, או אל כל מאכל. "היקדש" — כלום נטמא האחרון הזה, שהוא רביעי בקודש? דלחם ראשון, ונזיד שני, ויין שלישי, ושמן רביעי. נזיד — תבשיל, כמו "ונזיד עדשים" (בראשית כה). יין ושמן — של נסכים:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:10:2.english: And he touches with his corner - With that corner in which the creeping animal was, that is to say, the creeping animal itself. And perforce it must be so, for if it were because of the corner, which is a first-degree source of ritual impurity, the entire garment would also be a first-degree source, so why did the verse specify the corner? Rather, it is because of the creeping animal, as the creeping animal itself touched the bread, and the bread touched the stew, and the stew touched the wine, and the wine touched the oil, or any food. "Shall it be holy?" — Did this last item, which is a fourth-degree impurity in consecrated food, contract ritual impurity at all? For the bread is a first-degree impurity, the stew is a second-degree, the wine is a third-degree, and the oil is a fourth-degree. Stew — a cooked dish, as in "and a stew of lentils" (Genesis 25:34). Wine and oil — of libations.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:1:1.hebrew: דם התמצית - אינו ראוי לזריקה, דכתיב: "כי הדם הוא (הנפש) בנפש יכפר" — דם שהנפש יוצאה בו מכפר, ושאין הנפש יוצאה בו אינו מכפר. אלמא: נשפך כמים, אינו מכשיר — כדרבי יוסי בר חנינא:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:1:1.english: Exudate blood - It is not fit for sprinkling [on the altar], as it is written: "For it is the blood (the life) that makes atonement by reason of the life" — blood with which the life departs effects atonement, but [blood] with which the life does not depart does not effect atonement. Evidently, [although it is] poured out like water, it does not render [produce] susceptible [to impurity], in accordance with [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:2:1.hebrew: דאפי' בחולין לא מכשיר - כדמפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:2:1.english: As even with non-sacred [animals] it does not render susceptible - As [the Gemara] explains the reason [below].

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:3:1.hebrew: קיבלה מיניה ר' שמואל - לפירושא דהאי טעמא מרבי זירא: אמאי לא מכשיר דם התמצית? לפי שאינו קרוי דם. והקרוי דם קרוי משק', כדכתיב (במדבר כ״ג:כ״ד) "ודם חללים ישתה", ומכשיר, כדכתיב: "וכל משקה" וגו', ואוקימנא אהכשר; ושאינו קרוי דם — אינו קרוי משקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:3:1.english: Rav Shmuel accepted [it] from him - [He accepted] the explanation of this reason from Rabbi Zeira: Why does exudate blood not render [food] susceptible [to ritual impurity]? Because it is not called "blood." And that which is called "blood" is called a "drink" [i.e., a liquid], as it is written: "And drink the blood of the slain" (Numbers 23:24), and [a drink] renders [food] susceptible [to ritual impurity], as it is written: "And all drink [that may be drunk in any vessel shall be unclean]" (Leviticus 11:34), and we established [that this verse refers] to rendering susceptible; and that which is not called "blood" is not called a "drink."

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:1.hebrew: הורצה - קרבן לבעלים, דמרצה ציץ כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:1.english: Is accepted - The offering [is accepted] for the owners, as the frontplate effects acceptance, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:2.hebrew: במזיד לא הורצה - להיות בשר קרבן נאכל לכהנים, דקנסא הוא; אבל בעלים נתכפרו, כדאמרינן ביבמות בהאשה רבה (יבמות ד' צ.), דכיון דמדאורייתא מרצי נמי אמזיד, לא מצו רבנן למימר ליה: "זיל אייתי חולין לעזרה". קתני מיהת "דם שנטמא", אלמא דם קדשים, שהוא משקין בית מטבחיא, מקבל טומאה. אלמא משקין טומאת עצמן דאורייתא, ו"דכן" דיוסף בן יועזר — מלטמא אחרים הוא; וקשיא לרב:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:2.english: [If he did so] intentionally, it is not accepted - [That is, it is not accepted] so as to allow the meat of the offering to be eaten by the priests, for it is a penalty [imposed by the Sages]; but the owner has achieved atonement, as we say in Yevamot, in [the chapter entitled] HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 90a), that since by Torah law [the frontplate] effects acceptance even for an intentional act, the Sages are not able to tell him, "Go bring non-sacred [animals] into the Temple courtyard." In any event, [the baraita] teaches: "blood that became ritually impure," which proves that sacrificial blood, which is [one of] the liquids of the slaughterhouse, contracts ritual impurity. This proves that the ritual impurity of liquids themselves is by Torah law, and [the declaration] "they are pure" of Yosef ben Yo'ezer [means only] from transmitting impurity to other items; and this poses a difficulty for Rav.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:3.hebrew: ומשני לעולם טומאת משקין דרבנן - והך טומאת דם דרבנן היא. ודקשיא לך: הא העיד יוסף בן יועזר דגזירת רבנן לא אגזור אמשקי בית מטבחיא? — האי תנא לית ליה דיוסף בן יועזר:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:4:3.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Actually, the impurity of liquids is rabbinic - And this impurity of blood is rabbinic. And as for that which is difficult to you: Didn't Yosef ben Yoezer testify that the rabbinic decree was not decreed upon the liquids of the slaughterhouse? — this Tanna does not accept [the view of] Yosef ben Yoezer.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:1.hebrew: על הדם ועל הבשר ועל החלב - בין שנטמא הדם, בין שנטמא הבשר, בין שנטמא החלב — הציץ מרצה. ולא שיהא בשר טמא נאכל, דאין ציץ מטהר ודוחה לא תעשה ד"והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל", אלא לר' יהושע איצטריך, דאמר בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים עז.): "אם אין בשר אין דם", וקאמר הכא: ה"מ כשיצא בשר חוץ למחיצתו, שאין ציץ מרצה על היוצא, או שאבד הבשר; אבל נטמא בשר קודם זריקת דם — הציץ מרצה עליו להתיר דם לזריקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:1.english: For the blood, and for the meat, and for the fat - Whether the blood became impure, whether the meat became impure, [or] whether the fat became impure — the frontplate effects acceptance. And not that impure meat may be eaten, for the frontplate does not purify [the meat] and override the negative commandment of "And the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten" [Leviticus 7:19]. Rather, it was necessary according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who said in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 77a): "If there is no meat, there is no blood"; and [the Mishnah] states here: This applies only when the meat went outside its boundary, as the frontplate does not effect acceptance for that which went out, or if the meat was lost. But if the meat became impure before the sprinkling of the blood, the frontplate effects acceptance for it, to permit the blood for sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:2.hebrew: בין בשוגג בין במזיד - והאי דתני לעיל: ״בשוגג הורצה, במזיד לא הורצה״ — בכיצד צולין פליגי בה אמוראי: חד אמר, טומאתו — בין בשוגג בין במזיד, אבל זריקתו — בשוגג אין, במזיד לא; וחד אמר איפכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:2.english: Whether unwittingly or intentionally - And that which was taught above, “[If sprinkled] unwittingly, it is accepted; [if] intentionally, it is not accepted” — in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Tzolin, Amora’im disagree about it: One said, [the frontplate atones for] its impurity whether [it occurred] unwittingly or intentionally, but its sprinkling — [if done] unwittingly, yes; [if done] intentionally, no; and one said the reverse.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:3.hebrew: בין ביחיד - בקרבן יחיד. מזיד ורצון אחד הוא, אבל גבי שוגג שייך מזיד, וגבי אונס שייך רצון, ושוגג ואונס תרי מילי נינהו. וקתני מיהת על הדם — אלמא דם קדשים מקבל טומאה, וש"מ טומאת משקין דאורייתא, ולא רצו רבנן לטהר משקי בית מטבחיא, וקשיא לרב:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:5:3.english: Whether of an individual - [In the case of] an offering of an individual. Intentional and willful are one [and the same thing]; but regarding unwitting, [the term] “intentional” is applicable, and regarding circumstances beyond one’s control, [the term] “willful” is applicable, and unwitting and circumstances beyond one’s control are two [distinct] matters. And at any rate, it teaches [that the frontplate atones] for the blood — consequently, the blood of consecrated [offerings] contracts ritual impurity, and learn from this [that] the ritual impurity of liquids is by Torah law, and the Rabbis did not wish to declare the liquids of the slaughterhouse pure, and [this] poses a difficulty for Rav.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:6:1.hebrew: מדרבנן - וקסבר האי תנא דאמשקי בית מטבחיא נמי גזור, ודלא כיוסף:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:6:1.english: By rabbinic law - And this Tanna holds that they also decreed regarding the liquids of the slaughterhouse, and [this is] not in accordance with Yosef.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:7:1.english: And Aaron shall bear - [This] is written concerning the frontplate.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:7:2.hebrew: את עון הקדשים - פסול הקרבן יכשיר וירצה, ואינו מכפר על האוכלין אותו טמא, דעון הקדשים כתיב, ולא עון הכהנים:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:7:2.english: The sin of the holy things - [The frontplate] renders fit and effects acceptance for the disqualification of the offering, but it does not atone for those who eat it [while] impure, for “the sin of the holy things” is written, and not “the sin of the priests.”

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:8:1.hebrew: איזה עון הוא נושא - איזה פסול הוא מכשיר? "אם עון פיגול — הרי כבר נאמר: 'לא ירצה'", גרסי' בת"כ, "ואם עון נותר — הרי כבר נאמר: 'לא יחשב'". והכי פי': אם עון פיגול — והוא מחשבת חוץ למקומו, שנקראת פיגול, כדכתיב בקדושים תהיו: "ואם האכל יאכל ביום השלישי פגול הוא לא ירצה", ומוקמינן לה בזבחים בפ"ב (דף כח:): "אם אינו ענין לחוץ לזמנו, תנהו ענין לחוץ למקומו" — הרי כבר נאמר "לא ירצה" בקדושים תהיו כדפרשינן. ואם עון נותר — מחשבת נותר, ששחטו על מנת להותיר ולאכלו חוץ לזמנו — הרי כבר נאמר: "לא יחשב", "ואם האכל יאכל מבשר זבח שלמיו ביום השלישי וגו'" בפרשת צו את אהרן, ואמרינן בזבחים ובתורת כהנים: במחשב לאכול שלא בזמנו ביום השלישי הכתוב מדבר, וכתיב: "לא יחשב לו", אלמא לית ליה תקנתא. ורובא גרסי איפכא: "אם עון פיגול — הרי כבר נאמר: 'לא יחשב'", ומוקמינן ליה לפיגול חוץ לזמנו, שכן לשונו בכל הגמרא; "ואם עון נותר — הרי כבר נאמר: 'לא ירצה'", ומוקמי' ליה בנותר ממש. ולא יתכן: חדא, דלא כתב "לא ירצה" אלא במחשבת חוץ למקומו וחוץ לזמנו. ועוד, אי נותר ממש, למאי "לא ירצה"? אי לאכשורי קרבן — הרי כשר ועומד הוא משעה שנעשו עבודות דמו בהכשר, כדאמרינן בתורת כהנים: "או אינו אלא באוכל מזבחו ביום השלישי הכתוב מדבר? וכי אפשר לומר כן?! מאחר שהוכשר, חוזר ויפסל?!" ואם "לא ירצה" — לא יתכפר האוכל נותר קאמר, וכי יש כפרה לחייבי כריתות?! ועוד, "לא ירצה" — הקרבן משמע! ותו, מי איצטריך למימר דציץ לא מכפר על המחייב כרת? והא "עון הקדשים" כתיב, ולא עון האוכלים! וכלישנא קמא גרסי' בתורת כהנים, ועיקר הוא. והאי דקרי ליה להאי פיגול ולהאי נותר — משום דתורת כהנים מדרש הוא, ונקט לישנא דקרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:8:1.english: Which sin does it bear? - Which disqualification does [the Tzitz] validate? "If [it refers to] the sin of piggul, it is already stated: 'It shall not be accepted'" — this is how we read in Torat Kohanim — "and if [it refers to] the sin of notar, it is already stated: 'Neither shall it be credited.'" And this is its explanation: If [it refers to] the sin of piggul — and that is the intention [to consume the offering] outside its designated place, which is called piggul, as it is written in [the portion of] Kedoshim Tiheyu: "And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is piggul; it shall not be accepted" (Leviticus 19:7), and we establish this in Zevachim, in chapter 2 (28b): "If it is of no matter to [the intention of] outside its designated time, apply it as a matter to [the intention of] outside its designated place" — behold, "it shall not be accepted" is already stated in Kedoshim Tiheyu, as we explained. And if [it refers to] the sin of notar — [that is] the intention of notar, where one slaughtered [the offering] with the intention to leave [it] over and eat it outside its designated time — behold, it is already stated: "Neither shall it be credited" [in the verse]: "And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace-offerings is eaten on the third day, etc." (Leviticus 7:18) in the portion of Tzav et Aharon; and we say in Zevachim and in Torat Kohanim: The verse is speaking of one who intends to eat [it] outside its designated time, on the third day, and it is written: "Neither shall it be credited to him," which proves that it has no remedy. Most [texts], however, read the opposite: "If [it refers to] the sin of piggul, it is already stated: 'Neither shall it be credited'", and they establish piggul as [the intention of] outside its designated time, for such is its phrasing throughout the Gemara; "and if [it refers to] the sin of notar, it is already stated: 'It shall not be accepted'", and they establish it as actual notar. Yet [that reading] is not tenable: First, because "it shall not be accepted" is written only concerning the intention [to consume the offering] outside its designated place and outside its designated time. Furthermore, if [it refers to] actual notar, for what [purpose does the verse state] "it shall not be accepted"? If [it means] to validate the sacrifice — behold, it already stands valid from the moment the services of its blood were performed in a valid manner, as we say in Torat Kohanim: "Or is the verse speaking only of one who eats from his sacrifice on the third day? But is it possible to say so? Once it has become valid, can it become disqualified again?!" And if "it shall not be accepted" means that the one who eats notar will not be atoned for — is there any atonement for those liable to karet?! Furthermore, "it shall not be accepted" implies the sacrifice [itself]! And furthermore, was it necessary to state that the Tzitz does not effect atonement for one who incurs karet? Behold, "the iniquity of the sacred things" is written (Exodus 28:38), not the iniquity of those who eat! And as in the first version, we read in Torat Kohanim, and it is the primary [version]. And as for why it calls this [intention of outside its place] piggul and that [intention of outside its time] notar — that is because Torat Kohanim is a Midrash [Halakha], and it adopted the phrasing of the verse.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:1.hebrew: הא - כמו "הרי" — כלומר: הרי יש לך להבין על כרחך, שאין לך עון הקדשים שיוכל ציץ לרצות עליו אלא עון טומאה. ומאי שנא טומאה מפסול יוצא ושאר הפסולין:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:1.english: Evidently - [This is] like [the word] harei [behold / it must be] — that is to say: Behold, you must perforce understand that there is no sin of consecrated objects for which the frontplate can effect acceptance other than the sin of impurity. And how is impurity different from the disqualification of [that which has] gone out and the other disqualifications?

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:2.hebrew: שהותרה מכללה בצבור - דנדחית מפני קרבן צבור, דכתיב "במועדו" — ואפי' בשבת, ואפי' בטומאה. וכיון דהיקלתה אצלה, לכך היקלתה אף ביחיד: שלא הותרה אצלו לכתחלה בלא ציץ — ירצה הציץ עליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:2.english: Which was exempted from its general [prohibition] in [the case of] the community - For [impurity] is overridden for a communal offering, as it is written: “In its appointed season” (Numbers 28:2) — even on Shabbat, and even in [a state of] impurity. And since [the Torah] was lenient regarding it in its [the community’s] case, therefore it was lenient [regarding it] even for an individual: [in] that, [although] it was not permitted in his case ab initio without the frontplate, the frontplate effects acceptance for it.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:3.hebrew: מאי עון טומאה - לאו טומאת דם? דאין מצריך רצוי אלא א"כ נטמא דם שהכפרה תלויה בו, אלמא דם מקבל טומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:3.english: What is [this] “sin of impurity”? - Is it not the impurity of blood? For [an offering] does not require propitiation unless the blood became impure, upon which atonement depends; evidently, blood contracts impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:4.hebrew: לא טומאת קמצין - שהקומץ מתיר את המנחה כדם המתיר את הזבח, וכל הכפרה תלויה בו. והוא הדין דמצי לשנויי: "לא, בטומאת בשר וחלב", ואליבא דר' יהושע בעי ציץ, דאמר: "אם אין בשר אין דם", אלא ניחא ליה לאוקמיה כדברי הכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 16b:9:4.english: No, the impurity of handfuls - For the handful permits the meal-offering like the blood that permits the animal sacrifice, and the entire atonement depends on it. And the same principle applies that it could have answered: "No, regarding the impurity of meat and fat," and according to Rabbi Yehoshua it requires the frontplate, as he said: "If there is no meat, there is no blood"; but it preferred to establish it in accordance with everyone.

Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:1:1.hebrew: דם שאינו נשפך כמים אינו מכשיר - הקשה ה"ר יעקב דאורלינ"ש: א"כ, דם חיה ועוף דטעונים כיסוי לא יהיו מכשירים, דכיון דטעונים כיסוי — לא חשיב נשפך כמים; דאמרינן בפ' כיסוי הדם (חולין פד: ושם): "אמריתו חיה בכלל בהמה לסימנים, אימא נמי בהמה בכלל חיה לכיסוי", ומשני: "אמר קרא: על הארץ תשפכנו כמים" — אלמא דם חיה לא חשיב נשפך כמים! ולאו פירכא היא; דכל דם הנשפך כמים לארץ ואין צריך לקבלו בכלי, כגון דם חיה — הוקש למים לענין הכשר; וגם לענין כיסוי היה ראוי להקישו למים, אי לאו דגלי קרא להדיא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:1:1.english: "Blood that is not poured out like water does not render [produce] susceptible" - Rabbi Jacob of Orleans raised a difficulty: If so, the blood of a wild beast and a bird, which require covering, should not render [produce] susceptible [to impurity]! For since they require covering, [their blood] is not considered "poured out like water," as we say in the chapter [entitled] Kisui HaDam (Chullin 84b and elsewhere): "You say [that] a wild beast is included in [the category of] domesticated animal regarding the signs [of slaughter]; say also [that] a domesticated animal is included in [the category of] wild beast regarding covering [its blood]!" And [the Gemara] answers: "Scripture states: 'You shall pour it upon the earth like water'" — evidently, the blood of a wild beast is not considered "poured out like water"! But this is not a [valid] refutation, for any blood that is poured out like water onto the ground and does not need to be received in a vessel, such as the blood of a wild beast, is compared to water regarding the matter of susceptibility [to impurity]; and even regarding the matter of covering, it would have been appropriate to compare it to water, were it not that Scripture explicitly revealed [otherwise].

Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:4:1.hebrew: מדרבנן ודלא כרבי יוסי בן יועזר - ה"מ לאוקמא מדאורייתא, וכמ"ד טומאת משקין דאורייתא; אלא ניחא לאוקמא מדרבנן, וסבר האי תנא: מאי "נטמא" — הכשר, כמו שאמר רב:
Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:4:1.english: By rabbinic law, and not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben Yo’ezer - [The Gemara] could have established [the baraita as referring to impurity] by Torah law, and in accordance with the one who maintains that the impurity of liquids is by Torah law; rather, it preferred to establish it as [being] by rabbinic law, and [to maintain that] this tanna holds: What is [the meaning of] "it became defiled" [in the verse]? Susceptibility [to ritual impurity], as Rav said.

Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:5:1.hebrew: על הבשר - בפ' כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים עח.) אמרינן: לר"א, דאמר "יש דם אע"פ שאין בשר", הציץ מרצה על האכילות למאי הלכתא? לאקבועי בפגול, ולאפוקי מידי מעילה. ודלא כפ"ה, דפי' דלא את' אלא כר' יהושע: ה"ג ר"ת: "אם עון פיגול הוא נושא, הרי כבר נאמר 'לא יחשב'; ואם עון נותר, הרי כבר נאמר 'לא ירצה'". דהכי איתא במסקנא בהדיא בפ"ב דזבחים, דדריש תרוייהו מחד קרא אריכא דפרשת צו: ורישיה דקרא, דכתיב "ביום השלישי", מוקי למחשב לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו; וסיפא — במחשב לאוכלו חוץ למקומו. ובת"כ אהאי קרא דצו איתא האי גירסא. ורש"י הגיה איפכא על פי ת"כ דפרש' קדושים, דהתם ודאי דריש מקרא זוטא; ואותה בריית' נשנית לפי מה שרצה הגמרא בזבחים בתחל' ללמוד חוץ למקומו מקרא זוטא דקדושים. ולכל הפי', ק"ק: אמאי נקט עון פיגול ברישא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:5:1.english: "For the meat" - In the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (below, 78a), we say: According to Rabbi Eliezer, who says [that] there is [effective sprinkling of the] blood even though there is no meat, for what halakha does the frontplate atone for the edible parts? To establish [the offering] as piggul, and to remove [the meat] from [the scope of] misuse [me’ilah]. And [this is] not like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained that [our Mishnah] comes only in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua. This is the reading of Rabbeinu Tam: "If it bears the sin of piggul, behold it is already stated: 'It shall not be credited' [Leviticus 7:18]; and if [it bears] the sin of notar, behold it is already stated: 'It shall not be accepted.'" For so it is explicitly in the conclusion [of the Gemara] in the second chapter of Zevachim (29a), which derives both of them from the one long verse in Parashat Tzav: and the beginning of the verse, where it is written "on the third day," it establishes as referring to one who intends to eat it beyond its permitted time; and the end [of the verse, it establishes as referring] to one who intends to eat it outside its permitted place. And in Torat Kohanim on this verse of Tzav, this reading is found. And Rashi emended [the text to read] the reverse based on Torat Kohanim of Parashat Kedoshim, where it certainly expounds from the short verse; and that baraita was taught according to what the Gemara in Zevachim initially wanted to learn: [deriving intention] outside its place from the short verse of Kedoshim. And according to all the explanations, it is somewhat difficult: Why did it mention "the sin of piggul" first?

Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:9:1.hebrew: הא אינו נושא אלא עון טומאה שהותרה מכללה - תימה לר"ת: למ"ל שהותרה מכללה? תיפוק ליה דליכא לאוקמא לקרא אלא בהכי, כדמפרש: "אי עון פיגול וכו'"! ואור"ת: משום דקרא משמע דלא מרצה אלא דבר שיש לו היתר בשום מקום, דכתיב בסיפא דקרא: "לרצון להם". ופיגול ונותר נמי הותרו מכללם במנחת כהנים ובמנחת נסכים, דתנן בפ' ב"ש (זבחים מג: ושם) דאין חייבים עליהם משום פיגול; ועוד, דפיגול חוץ למקומו הותר מכללו בבמה. וכן משמע בהקומץ רבה (מנחות כה.), דפריך: "אימא עון שמאל, שהותר מכללו ביום הכפורים?", אמר קרא: "עון" — עון שהיה בו ודחיתיו; והיינו משום דאלרצון סמיך, וה"ק: עון שהוא לרצון. וא"ת: דהתם פריך נמי: "ואימא עון יוצא, דהותר מכללו בבמה?", ומשני: "'לרצון להם לפני ה'' — עון דלפני השם הוא נושא, ולא יוצא"; וא"כ, בפיגול דחוץ למקומו נמי נימא הכי, ומאי קאמר: "אם עון פיגול וכו'"? וי"ל: דיוצא ודאי אינו לפני ה', אבל מחשב להוציא — "לפני השם" קרינן ביה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 16b:9:1.english: "Evidently, it bears only the sin of impurity, which was permitted from its general prohibition" - Rabbeinu Tam is astonished: Why do I need [the rationale that] "it was permitted from its general prohibition"? Let [the baraita] derive it [simply from the fact] that it is impossible to establish the verse [as referring to anything] other than this, as it explains: "If [it atones for] the sin of piggul, etc."! And Rabbeinu Tam says: Because the verse implies that it effects acceptance only for something that has a permitted [counterpart] somewhere, as it is written at the end of the verse: "that they may be accepted" (Exodus 28:38). And piggul and notar were also permitted from their general prohibition in the meal-offering of priests and the meal-offering of libations, as we learned in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (Zevachim 43b and there), that one is not liable for them on account of piggul; and furthermore, piggul of [intent to consume the offering] outside its place was permitted from its general prohibition at a high place. And so it implies in [the chapter entitled] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 25a), where it objects: "Say [that it atones for] the sin of [service performed with] the left hand, which was permitted from its general prohibition on Yom Kippur?" The verse states: "iniquity" (Exodus 28:38) — an iniquity that was upon it and I pushed it aside; and this is because [the word "iniquity"] is juxtaposed with "that they may be accepted" [leratzon], and this is what it is saying: an iniquity that can result in acceptance. And if you should say: But there it also objects: "And say [that it atones for] the sin of [taking the offering] outside, which was permitted from its general prohibition at a high place?" And it answers: "'That they may be accepted before the Lord' — an iniquity that is before the Lord it bears, but not [an iniquity of] taking outside." And if so, regarding piggul of [intent to consume it] outside its place as well, let us say this, and why does [the baraita] say: "If [it atones for] the sin of piggul, etc."? And one can say: That which has gone outside is certainly not "before the Lord," but regarding one who has intention to take [it] outside — we [still] call this "before the Lord."
